alarm_removal_checks.signal: bk.C3sig -> strat.fam4 reads c.F through ov.macro_cond for the gate (inv, shock6m) and the caution tier (shock6m): all off

interpretation_caveat.what: In v1 the trend exit only fires while an alarm is on. Forcing alarms off therefore removes the trend exit itself, the caution cap and the brake warned mode: what is left is the volatility switch plus brake (on S&P 1955-85 that is a constant 3x). So the gap is the value of the alarm-switched exit, not of the alarm information alone.
interpretation_caveat.reading: S&P eras: an always-on trend exit gives 12.03% (1955-85) and 12.48% (1970-85) against v1 11.94% / 12.63%, so alarm information adds about 0 there. NDX 1986-2014: always-on exit 8.38% against v1 31.08%, so the alarm timing is worth about 22.7 points on the path it was designed on.

C3.verdict: REPRODUCED; near-equality of path and glued is genuine, not a bug

independent_checks.note: shock6m differs on 0.001-0.003% of days (a 6-month change of exactly 1.00 point is rounding sensitive); medians, quartiles and percentiles identical

why_genuine.explanation: path_flags keeps the original daily changes of the 10-year yield and the original yield spread, and re-accumulates them along the path. Inside a block the 6-month shock flag equals the original after 126 days; the inversion flag is a 378-day memory, longer than a 250-day block, so it smears across blocks (on 54% of days on the path against 39% glued in 1955-85). The two flag sets differ on 28-31% of days and the v1 signal on 11-12% of days, about as much as on the NDX pool (25% / 12.5%), where the same scrambling costs 10.9 points. In the S&P era it costs nothing because the alarm timing carries no extra information there: alarms are on 41-77% of days, and an always-on trend exit earns almost the same (11.7% / 6.0% median) as path (12.4% / 7.2%) and glued (12.0% / 7.0%).

caveats.power: Because both distributions coincide in this era, A6 cannot tell the path yardstick from the glued one: the real 11.94% sits at the 47th percentile of path AND the 49th of glued. It does not show that dev250_path (16.2%) is the fair central expectation for NDX.

horizon_1970_85.note: real path is 16 years, the claim compares it with 30-year paths; at a matching 16-year horizon the percentile is 74-75, not 82-85

caveats.pool: pools start 300 trading days before the era start (1953-10-21 and 1968-10-07), not exactly 1955 / 1970

C4.verdict: REPRODUCED; failure is real and not caused by a bug that hurts H1

minor_deviations_not_bugs: h1_run.py line 64: Rpx_f is built but never used; AMEND_A1 said the phenomenon test "also reports the price basis" and it does not

CAGR uses trading days / 252. In 1927-54 the market traded about 290 days a year, so that era is 27.5 calendar years counted as 31.7; per calendar year the sealed values are primary 0.0216 vs B0 0.0577 (1927-54) and 0.1233 vs 0.0965 (full). Fund fee, cash spread and the tax year also run per 252 trading days there. Ranking unchanged.
monthly drift rebalance to equal weight is not what hurts: trading only when the target set changes gives 0.1219 (real 1986-2014) and 0.0313 (path median)

sanity_sim_vs_real.reading: At 1x on real history the rule earns 8.5% against 8.7% for a static equal-weight hold of the same sectors; on the paths 5.4% against 8.7%. So scrambling alone costs about 3 points a year before leverage: the 252-day lookback is longer than the 250-day block, so the ranking mostly describes a different block from the one being traded. At 3x that loss is multiplied (static 3x equal weight 8.2%, rule 3.2%). With longer blocks the 3x median rises 3.7 -> 4.4 -> 6.2 -> 8.2% (250/500/1000/2000 days) toward the real figure on the same 21-day grid (median 8.9%).

timing_cross_check.what: market-trend benchmark 1986-2014, zero cost and zero tax, closed-form daily product with "decision at close s earns from day s+3" (no shared loop logic)

bugs_found.what: share_lt_hold1x compares each path with the pool-median 1x hold, not with the same path

stated_more_strongly_than_evidence: C1: "below the same-path 1x hold 30.2%" is 21.6% when actually paired.

C1: the 89th percentile is against the path yardstick, which removes alarm timing by construction; against glued it is 67th, under the pre-registered 75th-percentile line. "Lucky draw" holds on one of the two yardsticks.

C2: "alarms account for 18.6 points" measures the alarm-switched trend exit as a whole. In the S&P eras an always-on trend exit reproduces v1 (12.03 / 12.48 vs 11.94 / 12.63), so alarm information adds about nothing there.

C3: A6 cannot separate path from glued in that era (they coincide), so it is not evidence that 16.2% is the right central expectation for NDX. The 1970-85 percentile (82-85) falls to 74-75 at the matching 16-year horizon.

C4(c): -13.7 points and 3.4% wins are on the price basis, which removes 1.0-4.9%/yr of sector dividends (x3) while NDX loses under 1%. On total returns the primary median is 8.04%, the gap -8.5 points, wins 13.8%. v1 still wins.

C4(c): 250-day blocks cannot carry a 252-day ranking, so the simulation is close to uninformative about sector momentum; it is a harsh test rather than a neutral one. Direction is unchanged with 2000-day blocks (v1 28.2% vs H1 8.2% px / 12.3% TR).

C4(d): "S&P 1955-85 10.79% vs 11.94%" flips on a like-for-like total-return basis: H1 19.93% vs v1 14.44% (v1 on the French total-return market). 1970-85 stays v1 ahead (11.81% vs 16.28%), 1986-2014 too (18.19% vs 31.08%).

C4(b): era values depend on the decision day. On 21-day grids (21 phases) the primary beats B0 in 8/21 phases in 1927-54 (median 6.4% vs 6.5%), 21/21 in 1955-85, 8/21 in 1986-2014 (median 10.5% vs 11.7%); the month-end 16.26% for 1986-2014 is above every one of the 21 phases and the month-end 1.88% for 1927-54 is near the bottom. Only 1955-85 is robust. The fail verdict does not depend on this.
C4(d): the real 1986-2014 value 12.43% is at the top of its phase range (4.9-12.5%, median 8.9%).
C4(e): P = 2.4% is price basis; with H1 on total returns against v1 on price (upper bound for H1) it is 35.7%. Both are far under the 90% line.
